title: The 'pause for the migration' remedy halts every registered Phoenix contract; the granular workaround disables the circuit breaker
description: `pause()` is onlyPauser and the registered pauser is the ecosystem-wide Pauser contract, whose `pause()` halts EVERY registered Phoenix contract at once and whose `unpause()` is onlyOwner. Pausing this staker for a multi-slice migration therefore means halting the whole ecosystem for hours or days. Temporarily repointing `pauser` via `setPauser` for granular control disables the global circuit breaker for this staker during exactly the window in which its most sensitive operations run, and breaks the Pauser's register/unregister invariant (`Pauser.register` validates `pausable.pauser() == address(this)`).
impact: No value at risk. Two operational hazards: (1) AVAILABILITY — pause() is onlyPauser and the registered pauser is the ecosystem-wide Pauser contract, whose pause() halts EVERY registered Phoenix contract at once and whose unpause() is onlyOwner; pausing this staker for a multi-slice migration means halting the whole ecosystem for hours or days. (2) SAFETY-MECHANISM REMOVAL — temporarily repointing pauser via setPauser for granular control disables the global circuit breaker for this staker during exactly the window in which its most sensitive operations run, and breaks the Pauser's register/unregister invariant (Pauser.register validates pausable.pauser() == address(this)).
attackPath: 1. The sanctioned remedy for CLASS-006 is 'pause first, then migrate'.
2. Calling pause() invokes the ecosystem Pauser, halting every registered Phoenix contract.
3. The operator reaches for setPauser to get granular control.
4. The global circuit breaker for this staker is now off, and re-registration will fail the Pauser's invariant check.
likelihood: high IF the operator follows the sanctioned remedy for CLASS-006 rather than adding the poolState gate.
assumptions: The pause remedy is used in preference to the code fix.
justification: Low, escalated from the scanner's QA under D-10. It is more than informational — it has a concrete availability consequence (whole-ecosystem outage) and a concrete safety consequence (circuit breaker disabled plus a broken registry invariant). It is NOT Medium: no value is at risk, the halt is a knowing operator act (only its SCOPE is the surprise), and CLASS-006 has a free code-level remedy that avoids the pause entirely.
recommendation: Fix CLASS-006 in code (poolState gate on stake) so the pause remedy is never needed. If pause must be used, document the ecosystem-wide blast radius as an explicit runbook warning and do NOT repoint pauser.
